description: Capability for every project tab (`p-<pid>`, V2-3.2; V2-3.7: a CHILD WEBVIEW of the one `shell` window, so this names `webviews`, never `windows`: Tauri grants on a webview OR window label match, and a window match would hand these grants to every tab including Home and the strip — there is no `main` window; Rust creates each window, see windows.rs, and every command re-checks in Rust that its caller is a project window on its own server's origin). The webview loads the dev-server UI from a loopback http://localhost:<port> origin, which Tauri treats as REMOTE content — so app commands (github_sign_in / github_is_signed_in / github_sign_out / github_open_verification) must opt that origin in via `remote.urls` (Phase 28 / DDR-108/109). The port is dynamic (4399→4401 on collision), hence the loopback wildcard. SECURITY: the untrusted cross-origin canvas iframe (a different localhost port) cannot invoke despite the wildcard match — and note it DOES match it, since wry passes the calling frame's own URL into the IPC request. Two things stop it, and the second is the load-bearing one: (a) core init scripts are injected `for_main_frame_only`, so the iframe never gets the Tauri JS global; (b) `window.webkit.messageHandlers.ipc` IS reachable from every frame, so what actually rejects the iframe is Webview::on_message dropping any invoke whose `invoke_key` doesn't match the per-run random key — which the iframe never receives. Leg (a) alone is one API call away from being wrong; leg (b) is the invariant. None of these commands return the token either (the token bridge is loopback HTTP + key, not a Tauri command). Verified in the DDR-109 security pass and re-verified in the 2026-08-04 defender pass. BROWSER OPENERS: `open_github_url` and `open_cloud_url` are the only two ways the webview reaches the OS browser, and NEITHER is a general opener (DDR-054 forbids one) — each is zone-locked in Rust, not by its argument. `open_cloud_url` resolves the allowed origin per call from MAUDE_CLOUD_URL (default https://cloud.maude.sh), exactly as the sidecar does, and accepts only that exact origin or an https host inside its zone; a self-hoster changing the env changes both halves together instead of leaving Rust locked to a stale origin. EVENTS (V2-3.6 M5): only `core:event:allow-listen` / `allow-unlisten` — never `core:default` / `core:event:default`, whose emit + emit-to would let a page forge `shell://navigate`, `github://device-code`, `menu://action`, `shell://state` or `maude://deep-link` into another window. REMOTE (V2-3.6 N-M2): `http://localhost:*` only, because every project server and its canvas origin are `http://localhost:<port>` (the info file the shell trusts names nothing else), so a `p-*` window on a `127.0.0.1` listener gets no IPC at all; the navigation guard (windows.rs `navigation_allowed`) keeps the top frame on the window's own recorded origin. CALLER CHECKS (V2-3.6 N-M2): every command granted here re-checks its caller in Rust (label AND current top-frame origin), pinned by windows.rs `every_granted_command_checks_its_caller`; the canvas origin refuses to be a top-level page (canvas-top-level.ts) and every localhost listener also holds [::1] on its port (loopback-listen.ts, NEW-1). PROFILES (M2) are not granted here (Home-only in Rust; the debug e2e capability grants them for the identity scenario).
